author: Andrew Cruz
title: Long Island woman hoards over 150 cats in horrible conditions: DA - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Cruz ,
9 hours ago
GLEN COVE, N.Y. (PIX11) — A Long Island woman is accused of hoarding 166 cats and abusing them, according to Nassau County District Attorney Anne T. Donnelly.
Alena Horbatko, 54, allegedly allowed the cats to live in filthy and unsafe conditions, causing many of them to suffer from severe respiratory and eye infections, according to officials.
Get ongoing crime and safety coverage on our homepage “The filthy, cluttered condition of the defendant’s Glen Cove home was unsuitable for the dozens of cats and kittens she was breeding and dangerous for their health and the health of her two children,” said Donnelly. “These animals cruelly and unnecessarily suffered because of this defendant’s actions, but thankfully, through the efforts of my office and the ASPCA, they are on the path to finding loving homes.”
Nassau County SPCA also assisted in the recovery of the cats.
Police received a call on June 7 over a hoarding situation at Horbatko’s home in Glen Cove and reported an odor coming from the house, according to investigators.
In addition to the cats, officials found garbage and various items throughout the house, making it difficult to walk around. The home was declared unsafe to live in.
The following day, a strong odor was reported, and Hazmat officials detected ammonia levels so high it could cause severe infections in animals.
The defendant pleaded not guilty on charges that include more than 160 counts of animal cruelty, according to court documents. She was released on her own recognizance.
The court ordered a temporary animal ban and two orders of protection against the defendant.
Horbatko is ordered to return to court on Nov. 19 and could face up to two years in prison if convicted on all charges.
